GENERAL REQUIREMENTS

01 00 00-1
SECTION 01 00 00
GENERAL REQUIREMENTS
PART 1 -
GENERAL
1.01
SUMMARY
A.
General:  This Section includes General Requirements to be incorporated into the Project.
B.
Related Documents
1. General provisions of the Contract, including General Conditions, and other Division 1 Specification 
sections apply to the work of this section.
2. Section 01 11 00 Summary of Work
1.02
COMPLETE PERFORMANCE OF THE WORK
A.
Contractor shall furnish all labor, products, materials, equipment, supplies, scaffolding, and temporary 
facilities, and carry out the work in strict accordance with the Contract Documents and at the prices stated 
in the bid.  These prices are to cover all expenses incurred in performing the work required under the 
Contract Documents.
B.
Contractor shall perform all specified repairs and procedures per all requirements as stipulated herein and at 
all components of the project manual including the following "General Conditions" and "Specifications"; 
All Other Attachments, Drawings, Details, Exhibits and Addenda as listed at the Project Manual Index; All 
subsequent authorized revisions.
C.
Stipulations herein and at all referenced, attached and covering documents shall be integral and binding 
requirements to the Contract and Contractor's performance of work.  Contractor's bid submission and 
acceptance of the Contract indicates that all stipulations are understood and accepted.
1.03
CONTRACTOR’S PERSONNEL
A.
Prior to the start of work, all Contractor personnel responsible for its performance shall thoroughly 
understand the entire scope of repairs including all General Conditions, specified repair procedures, 
Manufacturers' installation requirements, and related documents.
B.
Foremen:  The foremen for the work of all Sections shall be on site daily during the course of construction, 
shall speak and read the English language fluently, and shall have had a minimum of five (5) years experience.
C.
Qualification of Personnel: Use adequate numbers of skilled workers who are thoroughly trained an 
experienced in the necessary crafts and the methods needed for proper performance of the work of all 
Sections.
D.
In acceptance or rejection of work, no allowance will be made for lack of skill or competence on the part of 
workmen.
1.04
IMPLIED STANDARDS
A.
Indicated work which is not fully specified (in detail) shall comply with applicable related standards of the 
Construction Industry and the Applicable Building Code. Contractor's compliance with recognized proper 
Industry and Construction Standards shall be an integral part of the work and General Conditions.
1.05
MANUFACTURER'S SPECIFICATIONS
A.
All materials shall be used in accordance with the Manufacturer's directions, including specific 
requirements and installation restrictions pertinent to adverse weather conditions.  Manufacturers' 
specifications shall be considered a part of these specifications.
1.06
WORK RESTRICTIONS
MARCY RESIDENCES
GENERAL REQUIREMENTS
04/03/2026-CONSTRUCTION DOCUMENTS
01 00 00-2
A.
Working Hours: Work shall be conducted only during hours allowed by the New York City Building 
Department; and as agreed to with the owner and building management.
1. All demolition and noise related work to be performed during normal work hours unless otherwise 
approved by the Owner.
2. All other work to be performed between normal working hours as defined by the Owner unless otherwise 
approved by the Owner.
3. Obtain approval from Owner to apply for After Hours Variance if necessary due to the nature of work or 
to maintain schedule.
B.
Existing Utility Interruptions:  Do not interrupt utilities serving facilities occupied by Owner or others 
unless permitted under the following conditions and then only after arranging to provide temporary utility 
services according to requirements indicated:
1. Notify designated building operations staff and Owner’s Representative not less than two days in advance 
of proposed utility interruptions.
2. Do not proceed with utility interruptions without Ownership’s written permission.
C.
Nonsmoking Building:  Smoking is not permitted within the building or within 25 feet of entrances, 
operable windows, or outdoor air intakes.
1.07
WARRANTY
A.
All equipment, material and workmanship shall be guaranteed to be watertight and to be free from defects 
and the Contractor shall promptly correct any required replacement.  If the Contractor fails to commence and 
continue correction of such defects, the Owner may, with prior approval of the Architect, have the required 
work done by others and recover from the Contractor the cost of making the same and damage, if any, 
resulting there from.
B.
Except where specified otherwise in individual specification sections, the period of guarantee shall be FIVE 
(5) years, from the date of acceptance of the work by the Owner.  The subject date of acceptance shall be that 
on which final approval by the Architect is given on the Contractor’s final invoice or the date on which the  
Contractor’s retainer is released, whichever is later.
1.08
EXISTING CONDITIONS
A.
The Contractor shall thoroughly familiarize himself with the existing conditions of the facades, parapets, 
windows  and  all  related  building  components;  with  other  buildings  and  adjacent  areas  affected  by 
performance of work, movement of men and materials, etc.; with all work requirements.
B.
If work-in-progress reveals conditions substantially different than expected based upon original construction 
documents or as indicated in these specifications, the Owner shall be notified immediately and the Owner or 
its representative shall be responsible for determining any necessary changes.
1.09
SUBSTITUTIONS
A.
Any proposed substitutions or other modifications to the work or performance of the work as specified shall 
be submitted as an alternate deduct in writing, complete with all pertinent data and information sufficient for 
evaluation by Owner or its representative.  Owner or its representative must review, approve, and authorize 
any such amendments prior to incorporation into the work.
B.
The necessity and nature of any miscellaneous changes brought on by authorized revisions shall be 
determined by Owner or its representative.
C.
Where the phrase "or approved equal" occurs in the Contract Documents, all substitute materials, equipment, 
or methods must be approved as equal by Owner and its representative.
MARCY RESIDENCES
GENERAL REQUIREMENTS
04/03/2026-CONSTRUCTION DOCUMENTS
01 00 00-3
1.10
WORK INCLUDES
A.
Work includes all labor, materials, equipment, and services to complete all specified procedures, roofing and 
related work, all necessary protection measures for safety and to preserve existing or adjacent work, together 
with all attendant cleaning and removal of debris.
1.11
LAWFUL EXECUTION
A.
All work is to be performed in accordance with all requirements of all Federal, State, Municipal and any 
other governmental agency or law having jurisdiction over this work and its performance.
1.12
GRADES, LINES AND LEVELS
A.
The Contractor shall be responsible for verifying the lines and levels, verifying the existing conditions, and 
laying out of the work as indicated on drawings so that it will agree with the established lines, levels and 
dimensions.  If there is any discrepancy between the lines and levels as established in the drawings, he shall 
notify the Architect in writing describing such discrepancy, and shall not proceed with any work affected, 
until he has received written instructions from the Architect.
1.13
MEASUREMENTS AND DIMENSIONS
A.
Before ordering materials or doing work which is dependent upon coordination with building conditions the 
Contractor shall determine all dimensions by taking measurements at the building and shall be responsible 
for the correctness of same.  If any discrepancies are found, the Contractor shall notify the Owner in writing. 
No consideration will be given to any claim based on differences between the actual dimensions and those 
indicated on the drawings unless written notice is received before the start of construction.
B.
Any discrepancies between the specifications and the existing conditions shall be referred to the Owner and 
the Architect for additional instructions before any work affected thereby is begun.
1.14
PROJECT MEETINGS
A.
Contractor, Architect, and Owner shall attend weekly on-site meetings as required for the purpose of 
discussing the progress and execution of the Work.  The proceedings of job meetings shall be recorded by 
the Contractor.
1.15
TEMPORARY FACILITIES
A.
General: Provide and maintain facilities, services and utilities required for the fullest and most efficient 
execution of the Work, including but not limited to those listed below.  Unless specified otherwise, the 
Contract sum shall include costs of obtaining, if required, permits, approvals and meters.  Remove temporary 
facilities to their original condition when no longer required or when directed by Owner.
B.
Power And Water: 
1. The  Contractor  shall  arrange  for  temporary  power  as  necessary.  All  cost  for  the  installation  and 
maintenance of temporary power shall be paid for by the Contractor, however, the cost of electrical current 
consumed shall be paid for by the Owner.
2. All connections for water required for carrying out the Work shall be provided by the Contractor, who shall 
install and maintain temporary water supply connections to the existing Building System and piping 
required for the proper performance of the Work.  All water shall be carefully conserved.
3. Contractor shall arrange for drinking water as necessary, at his own expense.
4. Under no circumstances shall Contractor personnel make use of electrical or water outlets at areas not 
designated for use by the Owner or its representative.
MARCY RESIDENCES
GENERAL REQUIREMENTS
04/03/2026-CONSTRUCTION DOCUMENTS
01 00 00-4
1.16
ACCESS TO BUILDING AND SITE
A.
Contractor shall maintain public access streets and sidewalks free from dirt and debris from construction 
operations and shall obtain permission and/or required permits for use of public thoroughfares.
B.
All necessary precautions shall be taken by the Contractor to avoid interference with the Owner’s operation 
of the site.
C.
Contractor shall provide and maintain all ladders, ramps, stairs, scaffolds, hoists, chutes, derricks, etc., as 
required for the proper execution of the Work.  All such equipment and apparatus and their construction and 
arrangement shall conform to the requirements of all governmental authorities having jurisdiction.
1.17
ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION PROCEDURE
A.
Designate one person, the Construction Superintendent or other, to enforce strict discipline on activities 
related to generation of wastes, pollution of air/waste/soil, generation of noise, and similar harmful or 
deleterious effects which might violate regulations or reasonably irritate persons at or in vicinity of project 
site.
1.18
SCAFFOLDING AND SIDEWALK SHED
A.
Contractor shall maintain scaffolding and/or sidewalk bridging as required by the NYC Building Code and 
by all other regulatory agencies having jurisdiction over this project and the location of work.  Contractor 
shall assume all liability and responsibility to verify the extent any and all additional protection required for 
tenant, worker, pedestrian and public safety, including all legal requirements for same.
B.
All scaffolding and/or sidewalk bridging required for the work of this contract is part of this contract and 
shall be provided at no additional cost to the Owner.
1.19
RIGGING
A.
As part of the Contract, Contractor shall provide all rigging and related equipment necessary to perform the 
work without any damage to any Building element.
B.
Contractor's rigging and staging procedures shall conform to all applicable Federal, State and Municipal 
Codes and Regulations including permitting requirements.
C.
Independent lifelines and safety belts shall be provided to and worn by all persons riding scaffolds and at 
pipe staging. Contractor shall install separate lifeline for use by Engineer / Architect for inspection.
D.
Contractor shall verify conditions of all Building elements to be used for rigging and pipe staging supports. 
Suitable precautions shall be used where required by possibly unstable conditions.
E.
Engineer / Owner’s Access: The contractor shall include for scaffold access by the Engineer and Owner’s 
Representative on a daily basis. Inspection shall be only as required to define scope and location of work at 
each drop and as necessary to assure proper execution of the work. The Consultant agrees to schedule 
inspections in a manner to minimize impact on the progress of work but reserves sole right to determine the 
necessity and frequency of inspections.
1.20
PROTECTION OF THE SITE
A.
The Contractor shall provide, maintain, and operate all protective features as required for the safe and 
orderly prosecution of the work as required by the Owner and regulations of all governmental authorities 
having jurisdiction.
B.
The Contractor shall adequately protect all Building areas, elements, lower levels, terraces, roofs, adjacent 
sidewalks, streets, grounds, parking areas and any other on-site, neighboring, private, communal or public 
building elements or areas that could be rendered unsafe or hazardous by the performance of work.
MARCY RESIDENCES
GENERAL REQUIREMENTS
04/03/2026-CONSTRUCTION DOCUMENTS
01 00 00-5
C.
Protection measures shall satisfy all governmental requirements and ensure the safety of all tenants, guests, 
building personnel, pedestrians and others who could be affected by the performance of the work.  
Contractor shall provide all labor, equipment and material to affect such protection measures in a manner 
acceptable to Owner or its representative as part of the base work.
D.
Contractor shall take all necessary precautions for protection of same areas/elements from any soiling, 
damage or adverse effects from the performance of the work and movement of men and materials.  
Elements, areas and appurtenances thereof include but are not limited to: all roofs, terraces, drains, gutters, 
walls, windows, doors, parapets, railings, grounds, walkways, sidewalks, streets, parking areas, communal 
and public areas, interiors, personal effects, hallways, stairways, elevators, Building maintenance areas.
E.
Contractor shall fully repair and restore or replace to the satisfaction of the Owner or its representative all 
other work, elements, and property which are soiled or damaged in connection with the performance of this 
work. All public interior spaces utilized by the Contractor for the movement of men, materials, equipment 
or debris shall be left in an "as found" condition to the satisfaction of the Owner at the close of each day’s 
work or at the time those areas cease to be needed for the contractors use.
F.
The Contractor shall furnish, install, and maintain adequate supports, shoring, and bracing to preserve 
structural integrity and prevent collapse of existing improvements and/or Work modified and/or altered as 
part of the Work.
1.21
MAINTENANCE OF WATERTIGHT CONDITIONS
A.
Contractor shall be responsible for maintaining the integrity of any existing waterproofing at all areas of 
work and shall insure that integrity before leaving the area.
B.
Contractor shall provide all temporary measures necessary to ensure that no leakage results from any work 
in progress.  Such measures shall be provided at the end of each work period and be sufficient for whatever 
period and weather conditions are expected until the completion of work.
1.22
MAINTENANCE OF SITE AND ADJOINING PROPERTY
A.
Contractor shall maintain the site, after order to start work.  Contractor shall not, however, have exclusive 
possession of site.
B.
No work shall proceed until Contractor has provided sufficient protection measures.  No work shall proceed 
until Contractor has insured that all affected Building Personnel and the Owner or its representative have 
been notified, that the hazardous areas have been secured and protected, that all personal affects have been 
removed or protected.
C.
Contractor shall provide highly visible warning signs and barriers for all areas to be restricted during the 
course of work: at work areas, at roof and terrace areas, at lower building and grade areas.
D.
As required for safety during daily work above, Contractor shall coordinate temporary closing of additional 
areas/entrances through the Owner or its representative.
E.
Contractor  shall  provide  prior  notification  to  Owner’s  Representative  and  Building  Operations 
Representative of upcoming work and necessary safety measures at all private, communal and public areas 
which could be affected by the performance of repairs.  The Owner's decisions and instructions as to access 
limitations are to be strictly followed.
F.
Contractor shall be responsible for the safety of the adjoining property, including structures, sidewalks, 
paving, curbs, fences, waste lines, water, gas, electric and other mains, pipes, conduits, etc., until the work 
of the Contract is completed and accepted.  Contractor shall at his own expense, except as otherwise specified, 
protect same and maintain them in at least as good condition as that in which he finds them.
G.
All pavements, sidewalks, roads and approaches to fire hydrants shall be kept clear at all times, maintained 
and repaired to serviceable condition with materials to match existing.
MARCY RESIDENCES
GENERAL REQUIREMENTS
04/03/2026-CONSTRUCTION DOCUMENTS
01 00 00-6
H.
Contractor shall be responsible for maintaining the project fully weather and water tight until work of the 
Contractor is complete and accepted.
I.
Upon completion of the work each Contractor shall thoroughly clean up all dirt and waste resulting from his 
work as required to restore work areas to the state of cleanliness existing before work began.  In general, 
cleaning requirements are limited to the removal of rubbish, spatters, stains, smears, foot tracks, etc. 
However, where work that causes the dissemination of dust has been performed, cleaning requirements shall 
include, in addition to the aforementioned operations, all other operations necessary to remove the dust.

1.02
DESCRIPTION OF THE WORK
A.
The furnishing of all labor, materials, equipment, services, and incidentals necessary for Work on Marcy 
Ave Residences, located at 185 Marcy Ave, Brookyn, NY 11211, as set forth in the Contract Documents 
which include, but are not limited to, the Drawings, Addenda and Specifications.
B.
Project Information:
1.
Project:
 Marcy Ave Residences
2.
Project 
Location: 185 Marcy Avenue, Brooklyn, NY 11211
3.
Client: 
Rivington Company LLC
C.
Abbreviated Written Summary:
1.
The work under this project can be briefly summarized, without any force and effect whatsoever on the 
contract, as follows:
a.
The project is the conversion of a portion of an existing office building, located at 185 Marcy 
Avenue. The existing building is approximately 72,000 gross square feet, with existing daycare 
and office uses. The project is on lot 6, block 2151, with a lot area of 13,784 SF.
b.
The project will convert existing offices into new residences on floors 03 - 06, and on a portion of 
floor 02. There will be 55 new residential rental apartments added to the building. Work includes 
common areas on the first floor for the residential lobby, reception, and mail and package delivery. 
Work also includes residential amenities and new mechanical rooms on the cellar and subcellar.
c.
The project include a horizontal extension of existing rooftop structures and reconstruction of a 
portion of the existing roof deck to house a new residential rooftop amenity. The project will 
include new equipment and distribution for HVAC, plumbing, sprinkler, standpipe, electrical, and 
fire alarm.
d.
Work in the existing tenant spaces, including a child care center, commercial offices, and building 
management offices, will be limited to the minimum work necessary to install new building 
services for residential spaces.
e.
The project will require a temporary certificate of occupancy.
D.
Type of Contract:
1.
Project will be constructed under a single prime contract.

indicates. Request clarification from Applicant of Record as required.

DEFINITIONS

Unit price is an amount incorporated into the Agreement, applicable during the duration of the Work as a

Work required by the Contract Documents are increased or decreased.
B.

cost of prescribed items not specified or located in detail.  Where a repair quantity is specified and not 
indicated by location on the project drawings, such work items (e.g.: masonry pointing, miscellaneous face 
brick replacement, etc.) shall be performed at areas designated by the Applicant of Record.

unit prices and to have this work measured, at Owner's expense, by an independent surveyor acceptable to 
Contractor.

Part 3 "Schedule of Unit Prices" Article contain requirements for materials described under each unit price.

based upon the relevant Unit Prices of those items in order to determine the net credit, if any, for unused 
Allowances or to bill the Allowances to completion (e.g.: the dollar value of unused brick repointing 
Allowance may be applied towards overage of brick replacement, to be calculated based upon the 
established Unit Prices of those Allowances).  The accounting of Allowances shall be totaled irrespective 
of the location where the work is performed, within the bounds of the originally planned rigging, 
scaffolding, protection, and other relevant measures to accomplish the work.

included in the Contractor's original bid, such costs shall be submitted by the Contractor based upon

established, such additional costs shall not be negotiable.

APPLICATION

1.07
CONSTRUCTION CHANGE DIRECTIVE
A.
Purpose: When the Owner and Contractor are not in total agreement on the terms of a Change Order 
Proposal Request, the Owner may direct the Architect to issue a Construction Change Directive, instructing 
the Contractor to proceed with a change in the Work, for subsequent inclusion in a Change Order.
B.
Description of Changes: The Construction Change Directive will contain a complete description of the 
change in the Work and designate the method to be followed to determine change in the Contract Sum or 
Contract Time.
C.
Records: Maintain detailed records on a time and material basis of work required by the Construction 
Change Directive.
D.
Submittal of Data: After completion of the change, submit an itemized account and supporting data 
necessary to substantiate cost and time adjustments to the Contract.
1.08
COORDINATION
A.
Revision of Schedule of Values and Application for Payment: Promptly revise Schedule of Values and 
Application for Payment forms to record each authorized Change Order as a separate line item.
B.
Revision to Progress Schedule: Promptly revise Progress Schedule to reflect any change in Contract Time; 
revise schedules to adjust times for other items of work affected by the change and resubmit.
1.09
DISPUTES
A.
Notification of Disagreement: Should the Contractor and Owner disagree about the value of the proposed 
change in the Contract Sum or Contract Time, the Contractor shall notify the Owner, in writing, stating the 
reason for the disagreement. Disagreement about the value of a Change Order does not relieve the 
Contractor of responsibility to proceed with the change as ordered and to seek settlement of the dispute 
under the pertinent provisions of the Contract Documents and in accordance with the provisions as 
specified herein.

1.06
REQUESTS FOR INFORMATION
A.
Definition: During the bidding process or progress of the Work, the Contractor may uncover situations for 
which they believe the Contract Documents are not clear in their requirements whereupon they may submit 
a Request For Information (RFI) to the Architect.
B.
Correspondence: Contractor correspondence related to the Work shall be addressed to the Architect.
C.
Conditions for Requests for Information: If, after issuance of the "Notice To Proceed" clarification from the 
Architect concerning questions which may have arisen during the course of the Work, the Contractor may 
initiate a process of standard form letters identified as "Request(s) for Information" (RFI) subject to the 
following conditions:
1.
The format of RFI inquires shall be subject to the review and approval of the Architect.
2.
RFI's shall contain specific reference to the project name, drawing number, detail number, 
specification section and paragraph number, schedule type, or other related document which is 
pertinent to the Contractor's inquiry. The date of referenced documents or drawings must be clearly 
identified.
3.
RFI's shall be numbered sequentially with the date of issue clearly noted. Each page of attachments shall 
be labeled with the RFI number and sequential page number. RFI's shall be submitted in an agreed upon 
electronic digital format and shall be forwarded to the Architect.
4.
RFI’s shall have attachments to provide detailed, legible description of the item needing information or 
interpretations. Such attachments may include field dimensions and conditions, sketches, descriptions, 
measurements, photos, Product Data, Shop Drawings, and/or coordination drawings. Attached 
drawings shall include dimensions, thicknesses, structural grid references, and details of affected 
materials, and assemblies.
5.
RFI's shall originate only from the Contractor’s designated single senior officer of the Contractor's on-
site staff.  RFI's submitted to the Architect by individuals other that the Contractor's designated senior 
officer will not be accepted.
6.
It shall be the responsibility of the Contractor's senior officer charged with signing RFI's to maintain an 
up-to-date electronic log of RFI's and to advise the Architect, in writing of the status and disposition of 
RFI's at the weekly progress meetings.
7.
RFI's shall not be utilized by the Contractor to solicit consideration by the Architect of a "substitution".
8.
RFI's shall not be utilized by the Contractor to request any extension of Contract time or to request any 
revision of Contract cost. If the Contractor believes that the response received from the Architect to 
MARCY RESIDENCES
PROJECT MANAGEMENT AND COORDINATION
04/03/2026-CONSTRUCTION DOCUMENTS
01 31 00-6
any RFI warrants adjustment of the Contract time or cost, he shall advise the Owner and the Architect 
in writing immediately upon receipt of the response.
9.
RFI's shall not be utilized by the Contractor to solicit clarification of comments that have been 
communicated to the Contractor by the Architect in the course of shop drawing review or the review of 
other required submittals.
10. The Owner reserves the right to assess the Contractor for the cost (based on time and materials) of the 
review process performed by the Architect and/or any of the Architect's or Owner consultants when 
RFI's fail to conform to the requirements stated herein, or in the opinion of the Architect, are 
unnecessary or frivolous (i.e.; the subject of the inquiry noted in the RFI is suitably and/or clearly 
addressed in the Contract Documents).
11. The Contractor shall submit RFI’s sufficiently in advance of the Work to be performed as it relates to 
the Construction Schedule such that the Architect has ample time to review and respond to RFI’s. The 
Architect will respond to RFI’s sequentially in the order they are received.
12. Any written or electronic procedure selected by the Contractor to solicit responses to questions which 
arise during the course of the Work shall be required to comply with the procedures stated in 
paragraphs above.
D.

1:00 p.m. will be considered as received the following working day.

f.
Requests for interpretation of Applicant of Record’s actions on submittals.
g.
Incomplete RFIs or inaccurately prepared RFIs.
2.
Applicant of Record’s action may include a request for additional information, in which case Applicant 
of Record’s time for response will date from time of receipt by Applicant of Record of additional 
information.
3.
Applicant of Record’s action on RFIs that may result in a change to the Contract Time or the Contract 
Sum may be eligible for Contractor to submit Change Proposal according to Section 01 26 00 "Contract 
Modification Procedures."
a.
If Contractor believes the RFI response warrants change in the Contract Time or the Contract Sum,

1.02
DEFINITIONS
A.
Activity: A discrete part of a project that can be identified for planning, scheduling, monitoring, and 
controlling the construction project. Activities included in a construction schedule consume time and 
resources.
1.
Critical activities are activities on the critical path. They must start and finish on the planned early start 
and finish times.
2.
Predecessor activity is an activity that must be completed before a given activity can be started.
3.
Successor Activity: An activity that follows another activity in the network.
B.
Cost Loading: The allocation of the schedule of values for completing an activity as scheduled. The sum of 
costs for all activities must equal the total Contract Sum.
C.
CPM: Critical path method, which is a method of planning and scheduling a construction project where 
activities are arranged based on activity relationships. Network calculations determine when activities can 
be performed and the critical path of Project
D.
Critical Path: The longest continuous chain of activities through the network schedule that establishes the 
minimum overall Project duration and contains no float.
E.
Event: The starting or ending point of an activity.
F.
Float: The measure of leeway in starting and completing an activity
1.
Float time is not for the exclusive use or benefit of either Owner or Contractor, but is a jointly owned, 
expiring Project resource available to both parties as needed to meet schedule milestones and Contract 
completion date.
2.
Free float is the amount of time an activity can be delayed without adversely affecting the early start of 
the following activity.
3.
Total float is the measure of leeway in starting or completing an activity without adversely affecting 
the planned Project completion date
G.
Major Area:  A story of construction, a separate building, or a similar significant construction element.
H.
Milestone: A key or critical point in time for reference or measurement.
I.
Network Diagram: A graphic diagram of a network schedule, showing activities and activity relationships.
MARCY RESIDENCES
CONSTRUCTION PROGRESS DOCUMENTATION
04/03/2026-CONSTRUCTION DOCUMENTS
01 32 00-2
J.
Resource Loading: The allocation of labor and equipment necessary for completing an activity as scheduled.

A.

1.

completion date, unless specifically authorized by Change Order.
C.
Activities: Treat each story or separate area as a separate numbered activity for each principal element of 
the Work. Comply with the following:
1.
Activity Duration: Define activities so no activity is longer than 20 days, unless specifically allowed by 
Architect. For construction activities that require three months or longer to complete, indicate an 
estimated completion percentage in 10 percent increments within time bar.
2.
Procurement Activities: Include procurement process activities for long lead items and major items, 
requiring a cycle of more than 60 days, as separate activities in schedule. Procurement cycle activities 
include, but are not limited to, submittals, approvals, purchasing, fabrication, and delivery.

"Submittal Procedures" in schedule. Coordinate submittal review times in Contractor's Construction 
Schedule with Submittals Schedule.

Startup and Testing Time: Include not less than 10 days for startup and testing.

Substantial Completion: Indicate completion in advance of date established for Substantial 
Completion, and allow time for Architect's and Construction Manager's administrative procedures 
necessary for certification of Substantial Completion.
6.
Punch List and Final Completion: Include not more than 30 days for completion of punch list items and 
Final Completion.

in schedule, and show how the sequence of the Work is affected.

3.
Work by Owner: Include a separate activity for each portion of the Work performed by Owner.
4.
Products Ordered in Advance: Include a separate activity for each product. Include delivery date 
indicated in Division 1 Section 01 11 00 "Summary of Work". Delivery dates indicated stipulate the 
earliest possible delivery date.
5.
Owner-Furnished Products: Include a separate activity for each product. Include delivery date 
indicated in Division 1 Section 01 11 00 "Summary of Work". Delivery dates indicated stipulate the 
earliest possible delivery date.
6.

a.
Coordination with existing construction.
b.
Limitations of continued occupancies.
c.
Uninterruptible services.
d.
Partial occupancy before Substantial Completion.
e.
Use of premises restrictions.
f.
Provisions for future construction.
g.
Seasonal variations.
h.
Environmental control.

2.07
CONTRACTOR'S CONSTRUCTION SCHEDULE (CPM SCHEDULE)
A.
Submission of a Practicable Work Schedule: The Contractor shall submit a practicable work schedule in 
reproducible form, showing the order in which the Contractor proposes to carry on the work and the time at 
which the several salient features will be started and completed.
B.
Presentation of the Schedule in a Network Analysis Format: Present the schedule in the form of a network 
analysis in accordance with procedures generally referred to as Program Evaluation Review Techniques 
(PERT) or Critical Path Method (CPM). This analysis shall include, as a minimum, a graphic representation 
of significant activities and events involved in the construction of the Project.
C.
Incorporation of Work Performed by Contractors in Network Analysis: The Contractor shall incorporate into 
the network analysis work being performed by subcontractors so that work involved is shown in the network 
analysis for the complete Project.
D.
Depiction of Sequence of the Activities Planned: The network graphic representation must clearly depict the 
sequence of the activities planned by the Contractor, their interdependence and time required to perform each 
activity. In developing the Project network, the Contractor shall use notation, either arrow or precedence, 
which shows the relationship of activities in a network diagram.
E.
Other Items to be Shown on the Network: Activities shown on the network shall consist not only of the actual 
construction operations, but shall also include the preparation , processing and submission of shop drawings 
and samples and reviews therefore, procurement of materials and equipment, fabrication and delivery of 
materials, installation and testing of major and critical items, contiguous or related work under other 
contracts, and other items pertinent to the Work. Related activities shall be grouped on the network for 
simplification. The selection of activities will be subject to review by the Architect.
F.
Tabular Listing of Activities Listed on the Network Analysis: The Contractor shall furnish with the initial 
network analysis a tabular listing of activities listed on the network analysis. For each activity there shall be 
listed the earliest and latest start times, the earliest and latest finish times, and the slack time. Activities on 
the critical path shall be so indicated.
G.
Information to be Included in a Monthly Report: During the progress of the Work the Contractor shall, by 
the fifteenth day of each month, submit a calendar monthly report on the Work progress. These reports shall 
be in tabular form and for each of the network activities shall include the following information:
1.
The actual start date of the activity.
2.
Time estimated to complete that activity.
3.
Past month's estimated completion date.
4.
Presently estimated completion date.
5.
Scheduled completion date.
6.
Actual completion dates of each activity as applicable.
7.
Items on the critical path shall be so noted.
H.
Narrative Report of the Construction Progress: In addition to the tabular report, the Contractor shall provide 
a narrative report on the construction progress and shall particularly note conditions that may delay progress 
of the Work. In the event of such delays, the Contractor shall describe actions proposed to overcome the 
adverse conditions to maintain the planned construction schedule.

1.01 
SUMMARY 
A. 
General:  This Section specifies administrative and procedural requirements for submittals required for 
performance of the Work. 
B. 
Submittals For Architect’s Action: Submittals which require the Architect’s responsive action are defined 
in this and other Specifications Sections, and include but not limited to: 
1. Shop Drawings. 
2. Product Data. 
3. Samples. 
C. 
Submittals For Information: Submittals which do not require the Architect’s responsive action are defined 
in this and other Specifications Sections, and include but not limited to: 
1. Calculations. 
2. Certifications. 
D. 
Related Documents 
1. Refer to General Conditions, for other requirements governing Shop Drawings, Product Data and 
Samples. 
2. Section 01 29 00 "Payment Procedures" for submitting Applications for Payment and the schedule of 
values.

Contractor shall coordinate a concurrent submittal of such products.

submittals until related submittals are received.

Architect Review of Submittals: The review of submittals by the Architect will be for general conformance 
with the requirements of the Contract Documents only and shall not be interpreted as a checking of detailed 
dimensions, quantities or approval of deviations from the Contract Documents. The Architect's review shall 
not relieve the Contractor of his responsibility for accuracy of the submittals nor for the furnishing and 
installation of materials or equipment in accordance with Contract requirements. The Architect's review of 
a separate item shall not indicate review of the complete assembly in which it functions. 
1. Review of submittals is not to be interpreted as an analysis of a substitute material or system nor 
utilized for a "Request for Information". Review of substitutions will be accomplished in accordance 
with the requirements set forth in Specification Section 01 60 00, "Product Requirements". Procedure 
for "Request for Information" shall be in accordance with the requirements set forth in Specification 
Section 01 31 00, "Project Management and Coordination”. 
2. Allow enough time for submittal review, including time for resubmittals. No extension of the Contract 
Time will be authorized because of failure to transmit submittals enough in advance of the Work to 
permit processing, including resubmittals. The Architect will review submittals with in 10 working 
days of receipt in the Architect’s office and will return them to the Contractor with the Design Review 
Stamp applied. Notations by the Architect which increase contract cost or time of completion shall be 
brought to the Architect's attention before proceeding with the Work. Failure to do so indicates the 
Contractor agrees that notations do not represent additional cost or time.

1. Shop drawings shall show in detail, materials, dimensions, thicknesses, assembly, attachments, relation

drawings, verify dimensions and field conditions and check and coordinate the shop drawings of any 
section or trade with the requirements of other sections or trades as related thereto, as required for 
proper and complete installation of the Work.

elsewhere as directed by the Architect to depict proposed solutions for tight field conditions. These 
composite shop drawings and field installation layouts shall be coordinated in the field by the 
Contractor and his subcontractors for proper relationship to the work of other trades, based on field 
conditions.

resubmit for verification that comments have been complied with.  If, for any reason, Contractor 
cannot comply with the notations, Contractor shall make revisions and resubmit as described for 
submittals stamped "C ACTION". 
3. "C - REVISE AND RESUBMIT" means that a portion of the submittal does not comply with the 
design intent of the Contract Documents and that fabrication, manufacture, or construction may not 
proceed. Contractor shall make revisions and resubmit entire submittal only revising portions as noted. 
4. "D REJECTED" means that submittal does not comply with the design intent of the Contract 
Documents and that fabrication, manufacture, or construction may not proceed. Submittals stamped "D 
ACTION" are not to be used. Contractor shall make revisions and resubmit.

SECTION 01 35 00 
ALTERATION PROJECT PROCEDURES 
 
PART 1 - 
GENERAL 
1.01 
SUMMARY 
A. 
General:  This Section specifies administrative requirements for Alteration Project Procedures. Perform 
Alterations and related work in accordance with requirements of the Contract Documents. 
 
1.02 
DEFINITIONS 
A. 
Remove: Remove and legally dispose of items except those indicated to be reinstalled, salvaged, or to 
remain the Owner's property. 
B. 
Remove and Salvage: Items indicated to be removed and salvaged remain the Owner's property. Remove, 
clean, and pack or crate items to protect against damage. Identify contents of containers and deliver to 
Owner's designated storage area. 
C. 
Remove and Reinstall: Remove items indicated; clean, service, and otherwise prepare them for reuse; store 
and protect against damage. Reinstall items in locations indicated. 
D. 
Existing to Remain: Protect construction indicated to remain against damage and soiling during alteration 
work. When permitted by the Architect, items may be moved to a suitable, protected storage location 
during alteration work and then cleaned and reinstalled in their original locations. 
 
1.03 
SCHEDULING 
A. 
Schedule: Before commencing any alteration or removal Work, submit for review by the Architect and 
approval by the Owner, a schedule showing the commencement, the order and the completion dates for the 
various parts of this work. 
B. 
Notification: Before starting any work relating to existing utilities (electrical, sewer, water, heat, gas, fire 
lines, etc.) that will temporarily discontinue or disrupt service to the existing building, notify the Architect 
and the Owner 72 hours in advance and obtain the Owner's approval in writing before proceeding with this 
phase of the Work. 
 
1.04 
SUBMITTALS 
A. 
Cutting and Patching Proposal: Where approval of procedures for cutting and patching is required before 
proceeding, submit a proposal describing procedures well in advance of the time cutting and patching will 
be performed and request approval to proceed. Include the following information, as applicable, in the 
proposal: 
1. Describe the extent of cutting and patching required and how it is to be performed. 
2. Describe anticipated results in terms of changes to existing construction; include changes to structural 
elements and operating components as well as changes in the building's appearance and other 
significant visual elements. 
3. List products to be used and firms or entities that will perform Work. 
4. Indicate dates when cutting and patching is to be performed. 
5. List utilities that will be disturbed or affected, including those that will be relocated and those that will 
be temporarily out-of-service. Indicate how long service will be disrupted. 
6. Where cutting and patching involves addition of reinforcement to structural elements, submit details 
and engineering calculations to show how reinforcement is integrated with the original structure. 
7. Approval to proceed with cutting and patching does not waive the right to later require complete 
removal and replacement of a part of the Work found to be unsatisfactory.

B. 
Services of a Professional Engineer: The Contractor shall retain the services of a Professional Engineer 
registered in the State of New York to provide design of temporary bracing, shoring, etc..., which may be 
required as part of alteration Work. 
1. It shall be the responsibility of the Contractor's Engineer to prepare detail drawings and associated 
calculations representing shoring, bracing or other temporary construction which may be required to 
maintain the structural stability and integrity of the existing construction during the course of the Work 
represented in these documents. 
2. Drawings and calculations prepared by the Contractor's Engineer shall bear an original signature and 
seal indicating the Engineer's New York State Registration. Duplicate copies of drawings and 
calculations shall be forwarded to the Contractor prior to commencing any of the temporary Work 
represented in those documents. The Contractor shall, in turn, transmit those documents to the 
Structural Engineer of Record for his review. 
3. The Structural Engineer of Record will review the documents only for how the shoring, bracing and 
other temporary construction interacts and affects the existing structure. The Structural Engineer of 
Record's review shall not be construed as complete check, nor relieve the Contractor’s Engineer from 
responsibility for errors of any sort nor from the necessity of furnishing any additional details or 
calculations which may have been omitted or required by the New York City Department of Buildings. 
 
1.05 
QUALITY CONTROL 
A. 
Contractor’s Quality Control Responsibilities: Contractor is solely responsible for quality control of the 
Work. 
B. 
Laws, Codes, Rules, and Regulations: Comply with applicable Local, State, and Federal laws, rules and 
regulations pertaining to the following: 
1. Alteration Work: Alteration work, including but not limited to the Federal Occupational Safety and 
Health Act and the Construction Safety Act. 
C. 
Protection of the Public: The protection of the public during alterations, including but not limited to, 
requirements for safety of operations, noise control, removal and disposal of waste materials, control of 
dust, dirt, pollutants, flammable materials, explosive materials, corrosive substances, protection against 
fire. 
D. 
Requirements for Structural Work: Do not cut and patch structural elements in a manner that would reduce 
their load-carrying capacity or load-deflection ratio. 
E. 
Operational and Safety Limitations: Do not cut and patch operating elements or safety related components 
in a manner that would result in reducing their capacity to perform as intended, or result in increased 
maintenance, or decreased operational life or safety. 
F. 
Visual Requirements: Do not cut and patch construction exposed on the exterior or in occupied spaces, in a 
manner that would, in the Architect's opinion, reduce the building's aesthetic qualities, or result in visual 
evidence of cutting and patching. Remove and replace Work, cut and patched in a visually unsatisfactory 
manner. 
G. 
Controlled Inspection: Alteration work which temporarily alters or diminishes the structural integrity or 
stability of the existing construction shall be subject to Controlled Inspection pursuant to the New York 
City regulation: "Promulgation of the Rules Relating to the Controlled Inspection of the Stability and 
Integrity of Existing Structures During Construction Operations", dated August 26, 1993. 
H. 
Clean Air Act 
1. Prior to commencement of alteration, removal or renovation work, and in accordance with the Federal 
Clean Air Act, the Contractor shall engage a Certified Asbestos Consultant to conduct an inspection 
and survey to determine the presence of asbestos on the project. As required by Federal Regulations,

provide notification to the Federal Environmental Protection Agency, utilizing EPA approved forms, 
not less than 10 days prior to the commencement of alteration, removal or renovation work. Provide a 
copy of notification sent to the EPA both to the Owner and Architect. The compliance with this 
procedure does not supersede local requirements concerning asbestos regulations and certifications. 
 
1.06 
PROTECTION 
A. 
Explorations and Probes: Make such explorations and probes as are necessary to ascertain any required 
protective measures before proceeding with alteration. Give particular attention to shoring and bracing 
requirements so as to prevent any damage to existing construction. 
B. 
Items to be Used for Protection: Provide, erect and maintain catch platforms, lights, barriers, weather 
protection, warning signs and other items as required for proper protection of the public, occupants of the 
building, workmen, and adjacent construction. Provide and maintain weather protection at exterior 
openings so as to fully protect the interior premises against damage from the elements until such openings 
are closed by new construction. Provide and maintain temporary protection of the existing structure 
designated to remain where alteration, removal and new work is being done, connections made, materials 
handled or equipment moved. 
C. 
Precautions to Prevent Dust: Take necessary precautions to prevent dust from rising by wetting demolished 
masonry, concrete, plaster and similar debris. Protect unaltered portions of the existing building affected by 
the operations under this Section by dustproof partitions and other adequate means. 
D. 
Fire Protection: Provide adequate fire protection in accordance with local Fire Department requirements. 
E. 
Obstruction of Walkways, Passageways, or Staircases: Do not close or obstruct walkways, passageways or 
stairways. Do not store or place materials in passageways, stairs or other means of egress. Conduct 
operations with minimum traffic interference. 
F. 
Responsibility for Any Damage: Be responsible for any damage to the existing structure or contents by 
reason of the insufficiency of protection provided. 
 
1.07 
WORKMANSHIP 
A. 
Performance of Removal and Alteration Work: Perform removal and alteration work as shown, with due 
care, including shoring, bracing, etc. Be responsible for damage, which may be caused by such work, to 
any part or parts of existing structures or items designated for reuse. Perform patching, restoration and new 
work in accordance with applicable technical sections of the Specifications. 
B. 
Property of the Owner: Materials or items designated to become the property of the Owner shall be as 
shown. Remove such items with care and store them in a location at the site to be designated by the Owner. 
C. 
Reinstallation of Designated Materials or Items: Materials or items designated to be reinstalled shall be as 
shown. Remove such items with care, under the supervision of the trade responsible for reinstallation; 
protect and store until required. Replace any material or items damaged in its removal with approved 
similar and equal new material. 
D. 
Property of the Contractor: Materials or items demolished and not designated to become the property of the 
Owner or to be reinstalled shall become the property of the Contractor and shall be removed from the 
Owner's property. 
E. 
Execution of the Work: Execute the work in a careful and orderly manner, with the least possible 
disturbance to the public and to the occupants of the building. 
F. 
Noise Producing Operations: Take necessary precautions to keep noise-producing operations (such as 
impact hammering, Carborundum sawing, compressed air machinery and the like) to a minimum. Select 
equipment which is of a quieter nature than others and enclose areas of operation with acoustical screens 
 
MARCY RESIDENCES 
ALTERATION PROJECT PROCEDURES 
04/03/2026-CONSTRUCTION DOCUMENTS 
01 35 00-4 
and partitions or other means necessary to accomplish reduction of noise. Equip motorized equipment with 
mufflers or other type sound control and blanket equipment with acoustical materials. 
G. 
Removal of Masonry: In general, demolish masonry in small sections. Where necessary to prevent collapse 
of any construction, install temporary shores, struts or bracing. 
H. 
Alteration Work: Where alterations occur, or new and old work join, cut, remove, patch, repair or refinish 
the adjacent surfaces or so much thereof as is required by the involved conditions, and leave in as good a 
condition as existed prior to the commencing of the work. The materials and workmanship employed in the 
alterations, unless otherwise shown or specified, shall comply with that of the original work. Alteration 
work shall be performed by the various respective trades which normally perform the particular items of 
work. 
I. 
Embedded Anchorage and Attachment Items: Cut out embedded anchorage and attachment items as 
required to properly provide for patching and repair of the respective finishes. 
J. 
Floor Finishes: Remove existing floor finishes complete down to original sound substrate in areas 
designated to receive new floor finishes. Patch and repair existing substrates with materials best suited for 
the intended use, to retain structural integrity and compatible with specified finishes. Gypsum based floor 
patching materials are prohibited. Level substrate patching to align with existing floor finishes or as 
required to align new floor finishes as shown. Where feathering is required to align finishes at different 
elevations, extend patching to the greatest extent possible to prevent sudden transitions in flooring surfaces. 
Follow manufacturer's written instructions for use of repair products. 
K. 
Removal Of Existing Resilient Tile Floor Coverings, Resilient Sheet Vinyl Flooring Or Cutback Asphaltic 
Adhesives: In areas where removal of existing resilient tile floor coverings, resilient sheet vinyl flooring or 
cutback asphaltic adhesives is required, comply with requirements of "Recommended Work Practices for 
the Removal of Resilient Floor Covering" as published by the Resilient Floor Covering Institute. 
L. 
Finishing and Cleaning of Existing Surfaces: Finish new and adjacent existing surfaces as specified for new 
work. Clean existing surfaces of dirt, grease, loose paint, etc. before refinishing. 
M. Repair and Refinish of Equipment and Fixtures: Where existing equipment and fixtures are indicated to be 
re-used, repair such equipment and fixtures and refinish to put in perfect working order. Refinish as 
directed. 
N. 
Roofing: Confine cutting of existing roof areas designated to remain to the limits required for the proper 
installation of the new work. Cut and fold back existing roofing and cut and remove insulation and other 
roof accessories in accordance with original manufacturer's written instructions. Provide temporary 
weathertight protection as required until new roofing and flashings are installed. Consult the Owner to 
ascertain if existing guarantees, warranties or bonds are in force and execute the Work so as not to 
invalidate such agreements.

PART 2 - PRODUCTS 
2.01 
MATERIALS 
A. 
Use of Materials that are Identical to or Compatible With Existing Materials. If identical materials are not 
available or cannot be used where exposed surfaces are involved, ascertain compatibility and then use 
materials that match existing adjacent surfaces to the fullest extent possible with regard to visual effect. Use 
materials whose installed performance will equal or surpass that of existing materials.

PART 3 - EXECUTION 
3.01 
PREPARATION

A. 
Meeting: Before proceeding, meet at the site with parties involved in alteration Work, including mechanical 
and electrical trades. Review areas of potential interference and conflict. Coordinate procedures and resolve 
potential conflicts before proceeding. 
B. 
General: Verify conditions in the field prior to the start of Work. If unanticipated mechanical, electrical, or 
structural elements that conflict with intended function or design are encountered, investigate and measure 
both nature and extent of the conflict. Submit report to the Architect in written, accurate detail. Rearrange 
alterations schedule as necessary to continue overall job progress without undue delay. 
C. 
Protection: Protect existing construction during cutting and patching to prevent damage. Provide protection 
from adverse weather conditions for portions of the Project that might be exposed during cutting and 
patching operations 
D. 
Examination of Existing Surfaces Before Cutting: Before cutting existing surfaces, examine surfaces to be 
cut and patched and conditions under which cutting and patching is to be performed. Take corrective action 
before proceeding, if unsafe or unsatisfactory conditions are encountered. Inventory and record the 
condition of items to be removed and reinstalled and items to be removed and salvaged. 
E. 
Shoring, Bracing, Or Support: Provide shoring, bracing, or support to prevent movement, settlement, or 
collapse of areas to be removed and adjacent facilities to remain. 
F. 
Coverage and Protection of Equipment And Fixtures: Cover and protect equipment and fixtures from 
damage and soiling during alteration work, including existing furniture, equipment and fixtures to remain 
or to be salvaged and stored. Erect and maintain dust-proof partitions and closures to prevent spread of dust 
or fumes to occupied portions of the building. 
 
3.02 
PERFORMANCE 
A. 
General: Employ skilled workmen to perform cutting and patching. Proceed with cutting and patching at 
the earliest feasible time and complete without delay. 
1. Alter existing construction to provide for installation of other components or performance of other 
construction activities and the subsequent fitting and patching required to restore surfaces to their 
original condition. 
 
3.03 
DEMOLITION OPERATION 
A. 
Demolition Work: Demolition work shall be as shown on the Drawings. Do work required in connection 
with this Project with due care, including shoring, bracing, etc. Be responsible for any damage which may 
be caused by such work to any part or parts of existing structures to remain. 
B. 
Property of the Owner: Materials or items designated to remain the property of the Owner shall be removed 
with care and stored in a location on the site to be designated by the Owner. 
C. 
Property of the Contractor: Materials or items demolished and not designated to become the property of the 
Owner shall become the property of the Contractor and shall be removed from the Owner's property. 
D. 
Manner of the Demolition Work: Execute the work in a careful and orderly manner, with the least possible 
disturbance to the public. Proceed with alteration work in systematic manner, from top of structure to 
ground. Complete alteration work above each floor or tier before disturbing supporting members on lower 
levels. 
E. 
Removal of Steel Framing Members and Demolition of Masonry and Concrete: Remove steel framing 
members individually and lower to ground by hoists, derricks, or other suitable methods. In general, 
demolish masonry and concrete in small sections. 
F. 
Prevention of Collapse: Where necessary to prevent collapse of any construction, install temporary shores, 
struts or bracing. Do not commence alteration work until temporary construction is complete. 
 
MARCY RESIDENCES 
ALTERATION PROJECT PROCEDURES 
04/03/2026-CONSTRUCTION DOCUMENTS 
01 35 00-6 
G. 
Compliance of Requirements for Cutting and Capping Existing Service Piping: Existing service piping, 
including sewer, water and gas lines shall be cut and capped and electric, telephone and other wires shall be 
cut in compliance with the requirements of the local Public Utility Corporations and of City Departments 
having jurisdiction. Before cutting in on the above services notify the proper officials, persons or 
corporations owning same, obtain instructions for carrying out the Work and take precautionary measures 
they may deem necessary. Evidence of the discontinuation of these services shall be furnished in the form 
of proper releases from the appropriate agencies. Any individual water taps and electrical lines used for 
alteration purposes shall be shut off as soon as alteration work is completed and similar evidence of the 
discontinuation of such temporary services shall be furnished to the Owner. 
 
3.04 
CUTTING AND PATCHING 
A. 
Cutting: Cut existing construction using methods least likely to damage elements to be retained or 
adjoining construction. Where possible review proposed procedures with the original installer; comply with 
the original installer's recommendations. 
1. In general, where cutting is required use hand or small power tools designed for sawing or grinding, 
not hammering or chopping. Cut holes and slots neatly to size required with minimum disturbance of 
adjacent surfaces. Cover openings when not in use with temporary protection. 
2. To avoid marring existing finished surfaces, cut or drill from the exposed or finished side into 
concealed surfaces. 
3. Comply with requirements of applicable Sections of Division-2 where cutting and patching requires 
excavating and backfilling. 
4. Where services are shown or required to be removed, relocated or abandoned, by-pass utility services 
including pipe or conduit, before cutting. Cut-off pipe or conduit in walls or partitions to be removed. 
Cap, valve or plug and seal the remaining portion of pipe or conduit to prevent entrance of moisture or 
other foreign matter after by-passing and cutting. 
B. 
Patching: Patch with durable seams that are as invisible as possible. Comply with specified tolerances. 
1. Where feasible, inspect and test patched areas to demonstrate integrity of the installation. 
2. Restore exposed finishes of patched areas and extend finish restoration into retained adjoining 
construction in a manner that will eliminate evidence of patching and refinishing. 
3. Where removal of walls or partitions extends from one finished area into another, patch and repair 
floor and wall surfaces in the new space to provide an even surface of uniform color and appearance. If 
necessary, remove existing floor and wall coverings and replace with new materials to achieve uniform 
color and appearance. 
4. Where patching occurs in a smooth painted surface, extend final paint coat over entire unbroken 
surface area containing the patch, after the patched area has received primer and second coat. 
C. 
Patch, repair or re-hang existing ceilings as necessary to provide an even plane surface of uniform 
appearance. 
 
3.05 
SALVAGED MATERIALS 
A. 
General: Remove carefully to avoid damages. Materials for reuse on this project are to be incorporated into 
new work as shown. Except for items indicated to be retained as Owner's property, other removed and 
salvaged materials not indicated for reuse shall become Contractor's property and removed from site with 
further disposition at Contractor's option.

DISPOSAL OF DEMOLISHED MATERIALS

General: Remove weekly from site accumulated debris, rubbish, and other materials resulting from

B. 
Removal: Transport materials removed from demolished structures and legally dispose off site. 
 
 
3.07 
CLEANING 
A. 
Instructions: Thoroughly clean areas and spaces used for access and areas where alteration work has been 
performed. Completely remove paint, mortar, oils, putty and items of similar nature. Thoroughly clean 
piping, conduit and other items before painting or finishing surfaces. Restore damaged pipe covering to its 
original condition. 
B. 
Removal of Debris: Remove debris as the work progresses. Maintain the premises in a neat and clean 
condition.

PART 1 -
GENERAL
1.01
SUMMARY
A.
General:  This Section describes References used in the Contract Documents.
1.02
STANDARDS
A.
Standard Specifications: References to codes, specifications and standards referred to in the Contract 
Documents shall mean, and are intended to be, the latest edition, amendment or revision of such reference 
standard in effect as of the date of these Contract Documents. If such standard specifications are revised 
prior to completion of any part of the Work to which such revision would pertain, the Contractor may, if 
acceptable to the Architect, perform such Work in accordance with the revised standard specifications.
B.
Availability: The standard specifications, except as modified in the Specifications for the Project, shall 
have full force and effect as though printed in the Contract Documents. The standard specifications are not 
furnished with the Contract Documents, because it is assumed that the manufacturers and trades involved 
are familiar with their requirements. Upon request, the Architect will furnish information about where to 
obtain copies of the referenced standard specifications
C.
Applicability of Standards: Except where the Contract Documents include more stringent requirements, 
applicable construction industry standards have the same force and effect as if bound or copied directly into 
the Contract Documents to the extent referenced. Such standards are made a part of the Contract 
Documents by reference.
D.
Conflicting Requirements: Where compliance with two or more standards is specified, and the standards 
may establish different or conflicting requirements for minimum quantities or quality levels, refer 
requirements that are different, but apparently equal, and uncertainties to the Architect for a decision before 
proceeding.
E.
Minimum Quantity or Quality Levels: The quantity or quality level shown or specified shall be the 
minimum provided or performed. The actual installation may comply exactly with the minimum quantity or 
quality specified, or it may exceed the minimum within reasonable limits. To comply with these 
requirements, indicated numeric values are minimum or maximum, as appropriate, for the context of the 
requirements. Refer uncertainties to Architect for a decision before proceeding.
F.
Copies of Standards: Each entity engaged in construction on the Project is required to be familiar with 
industry standards applicable to that entity's construction activity. Copies of applicable standards are not 
bound with the Contract Documents.
G.
Copies from the Publication Source: Where copies of standards are needed for performance of a required 
construction activity, the Contractor shall obtain copies directly from the publication source.
1.03
DEFINITIONS
A.
Where "as shown", "as indicated", "as detailed" or words of similar import are used, it shall be understood 
that reference to the Drawings accompanying the Specifications is made unless otherwise stated. Where "as 
directed", "as required", "as authorized", "as reviewed", "as accepted" or words of similar import are used, 
it shall be understood that the direction, requirement, permission, authorization, review, or acceptance of 
the Architect is intended, unless otherwise stated.
B.
As used in the Contract Documents, "provide" shall be understood to mean "provide complete in place", 
that is, "furnish and install".
MARCY RESIDENCES
REFERENCES
04/03/2026-CONSTRUCTION DOCUMENTS
01 42 00-2
C.
The term "furnish" is used to mean "supply and deliver to the Project site, ready for unloading, unpacking, 
assembly, installation, and similar operations."
D.
The term "install" is used to describe operations at project site including the actual "unloading, unpacking, 
assembly, erection, placing, anchoring, applying, working to dimension, finishing, curing, protecting, 
cleaning, and similar operations."
E.
The term "Regulations" includes laws, ordinances, statutes, and lawful orders issued by authorities having 
jurisdiction, as well as rules, conventions, and agreements within the construction industry that control 
performance of the Work.
F.
Use of titles such as "carpentry" is not intended to imply that certain construction activities must be 
performed by accredited or unionized individuals of a corresponding generic name, such as "carpenter." It 
also does not imply that requirements specified apply exclusively to tradespersons of the corresponding 
generic name.
G.
The term "Project Site" is defined as the space available to the Contractor for performance of construction 
activities, either exclusively or in conjunction with others performing other work as part of the Project. The 
extent of the Project Site is shown on the Drawings and may or may not be identical with the description of 
the land on which the Project is to be built.
H.
A "testing laboratory" is an independent entity with the experience and capability to conduct testing and 
inspecting indicated, as documented by ASTM E548, and that specializes in types of tests and inspections 
to be performed and is engaged to perform specific inspections or tests, either at the Project Site or 
elsewhere, and to report on and, if required, to interpret results of those inspections or tests.
I.
The term “Professional Engineer” is defined as the entity who is legally qualified to practice in the 
jurisdiction where the Project is located and who is experienced in providing engineering services of the 
kind indicated. Engineering services are defined as those performed for installations of the system, 
assembly, or product that are similar to those indicated for this Project in material, design, and extent.
J.
The term "Installer" is defined as the Contractor or another entity engaged by the Contractor, either as an 
employee, subcontractor, or contractor of lower tier, to perform a particular construction activity, including 
installation, erection, application, or similar operations. Installers are required to be experienced in the 
operations they are engaged to perform.
K.
The term "experienced," when used with the term "installer," means having successfully completed a 
minimum of five previous projects similar in size and scope to this Project; being familiar with the special 
requirements indicated; and having complied with requirements of authorities having jurisdiction.
L.
Assigning Specialists: Certain Sections of the Specifications require that specific construction activities 
shall be performed by specialists who are recognized experts in those operations. The specialists must be 
engaged for those activities, and their assignments are requirements over which the Contractor has no 
option. However, the ultimate responsibility for fulfilling contract requirements remains with the 
Contractor. This requirement shall not be interpreted to conflict with enforcing building codes and similar 
regulations governing the Work. It is also not intended to interfere with local trade-union jurisdictional 
settlements and similar conventions.
M.
The term “factory-authorized service representative” is an authorized representative of a manufacturer who 
is trained and approved by the manufacturer to inspect and approve the installation of manufacturer's 
products that are similar in material, design, and extent to those indicated for this Project and who is 
authorized by the manufacturer to confirm the issuance of appropriate warranties.

A.
Specification Format: These Specifications are organized into Divisions and Sections based on the 
Construction Specifications Institute's 16-Division format.
B.
Specification Content: This Specification uses certain conventions in the use of language and the intended 
meaning of certain terms, words, and phrases when used in particular situations or circumstances. These 
conventions are explained as follows:
C.

the Contract Documents. Sections in the Project Manual are in numeric sequence; however, the sequence is

be interpolated as the sense required. Singular words will be interpreted as plural and plural words 
interpreted as singular where applicable and the context of the Contract Documents so indicates.
E.
Specification Language: Imperative and streamlined language is used generally in the Specifications. 
Requirements expressed in the imperative mood are to be performed by the Contractor. At certain locations 
in the text, for clarity, subjective language is used to describe responsibilities that must be fulfilled 
indirectly by the Contractor, or by others when so noted. The words "shall be" shall be included by 
inference wherever a colon (:) is used within a sentence or phrase.

01 45 00-1
SECTION 01 45 00
QUALITY CONTROL
PART 1 -
GENERAL
1.01
SUMMARY
A.
General:  This Section specifies administrative and procedural requirements for Quality Control.
B.
Testing and inspection services are required to verify compliance with requirements specified or indicated. 
These services do not relieve Contractor of responsibility for compliance with the Contract Document 
requirements.
1.
Specific quality-assurance and quality-control requirements for individual work results are specified in 
their respective Specification Sections. Requirements in individual Sections may also cover production 
of standard products.
2.
Specified tests, inspections, and related actions do not limit Contractor's other quality-assurance and 
quality-control procedures that facilitate compliance with the Contract Document requirements.
3.
Requirements for Contractor to provide quality-assurance and quality-control services required by 
Applicant of Record, Owner, or authorities having jurisdiction are not limited by provisions of this 
Section.
C.
Related Requirements:
1.
Section 01 22 00 Unit Prices and Allowances for testing and inspection allowances.
2.
Section 01 33 00 Submittal Procedures for specific submittal requirements.
1.02
DEFINITIONS
A.
Quality-Assurance Services: Activities, actions, and procedures performed before and during execution of 
the Work to guard against defects and deficiencies and substantiate that proposed construction will comply 
with requirements.
B.
Quality-Control Services: Tests, inspections, procedures, and related actions during and after execution of 
the Work to evaluate that actual products incorporated into the Work and completed construction comply 
with requirements.
C.
Mockups: Full-size, physical assemblies that are constructed on-site. Mockups are used to verify selections 
made under sample submittals, to demonstrate aesthetic effects and, where indicated, qualities of materials 
and execution, to review construction, coordination, testing, or operation, and to perform preconstruction 
testing to determine system performance. They are not Samples. Approved mockups establish the standard 
by which the Work will be judged.
1.
Product Mockups: Mockups that may include multiple products, materials, or systems specified in a 
single Section.
2.
In-Place Mockups: Mockups constructed on-site in their actual final location as part of permanent 
construction.
3.
Laboratory Mockups: Full-size, physical assemblies that are constructed at testing facility to verify 
performance characteristics.
D.
Preconstruction Testing: Tests and inspections that are performed specifically for the Project before 
products and materials are incorporated into the Work to verify performance or compliance with specified 
criteria. Unless otherwise indicated, copies of reports of tests or inspections performed for other than the 
Project do not meet this definition.
E.
Product Testing: Tests and inspections that are performed by an independent testing agency, qualified to 
conduct product testing and acceptable to authorities having jurisdiction, to establish product performance 
and compliance with industry standards.
MARCY RESIDENCES
QUALITY CONTROL
04/03/2026-CONSTRUCTION DOCUMENTS
01 45 00-2
F.
Source Quality-Control Testing: Tests and inspections that are performed at the source, i.e., plant, mill, 
factory, or shop.
G.
Field Quality-Control Testing: Tests and inspections that are performed on-site for installation of the Work 
and for completed Work.
H.
Testing Agency: A nationally recognized testing laboratory (NRTL) in accordance with 29 CFR 1910.7, a 
testing agency accredited in accordance with NIST's National Voluntary Laboratory Accreditation Program 
(NVLAP), or by a testing agency qualified to conduct product testing and acceptable to authorities having 
jurisdiction engaged to perform specific tests, inspections, or both. Testing laboratory shall mean the same 
as testing agency.
I.
Installer/Applicator/Erector: Contractor or another entity engaged by Contractor as an employee, 
Subcontractor, or Sub-subcontractor, to perform a particular construction operation, including installation, 
erection, application, and similar operations.
J.
Using a term such as "carpentry" does not imply that certain construction activities must be performed by 
accredited or unionized individuals of a corresponding generic name, such as "carpenter." It also does not 
imply that requirements specified apply exclusively to tradespeople of the corresponding generic name.
K.
Experienced: When used with an entity or individual, "experienced," unless otherwise further described, 
means having successfully completed a minimum of ten previous projects similar in nature, size, and extent 
to this Project; being familiar with special requirements indicated; and having complied with requirements 
of authorities having jurisdiction.
